_comment: Options for the ndX 'Optimize FRET calibration' action. The factor toggles are the point: the calibration always runs in full, but only the selected factors are written into the window, so a gamma determined on a reference sample is not replaced by a worse one fitted from this measurement's own populations.

sections.title: Determine
sections.description: Which correction factors this calibration is allowed to change. The others keep the value the window already has.

sections.label: α leakage
sections.description: Donor emission detected in the acceptor channel. Taken from the donor-only population, so it needs one.

sections.label: δ direct excitation
sections.description: Acceptor excited by the donor laser. Taken from the acceptor-only population, so it needs one.

sections.label: γ detection / QY
sections.description: Detection efficiency times quantum-yield ratio. From the 1/S = Ω + Σ·E fit across FRET sub-populations, or from the donor lifetime. Turn this off to keep a γ you determined on a reference sample.

sections.label: β excitation flux
sections.description: Ratio of the two lasers' excitation flux and cross-sections. Comes from the same E-S fit as γ.

sections.label: R₀ Förster radius
sections.description: Not a correction factor — it converts efficiency to distance. Off by default: it belongs to the dye pair and its environment, not to this measurement.

sections.label: γ from
sections.description: 'es' is the 1/S = Ω + Σ·E fit and needs at least two FRET sub-populations; 'lifetime' uses the static FRET line and works on a single population, but needs a per-burst donor lifetime and a trustworthy τ_D(0); 'combined' is the precision-weighted mean; 'auto' takes the E-S fit and falls back to the lifetime. The two routes are independent, so their disagreement is itself a diagnostic.

sections.label: Use light-path priors
sections.description: Combine the data estimates with the optical model's excitation/emission probabilities, so the result is a posterior: data where the data speaks, optics where it does not.

sections.label: Bootstrap resamples
sections.description: Resamples used for the factor uncertainties, with the population assignment held fixed. 0 skips them. It is cheap — the classification, not the resampling, is what costs.

sections.label: τ_D(0) (ns)
sections.description: Donor-only lifetime, which anchors the static FRET line. Only used by the lifetime route; a wrong value there shows up as γ disagreeing between the two routes.

sections.label: Linker σ (Å)
sections.description: Width of the dye-linker distance distribution, which sets the curvature of the static FRET line.

sections.label: Add accurate E / S / R_DA columns
sections.description: Write the corrected per-burst columns under new names. Not redundant with applying the constants: ndX's own efficiency equation has no direct-excitation term, so constants alone cannot make its native column accurate. Its own columns are left untouched.
